data.narrative:
Palantir is a public-stage AI & Software company with a current market capitalization of $312.5B and over $3B raised pre-IPO. The AI & Software sector contains 11 total peers, comprising 1 public company (PLTR itself) and 8 private firms. The identifiable private-stage peers include Figure AI, Scale AI, Reflection AI, Applied Intuition, and Skild AI, though these represent a fragmented set across different funding rounds and valuations rather than a cohesive comparable universe.

Standard peer-median triangulation is not applicable to this valuation given the composition of available comparables. No subset of same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier companies yielded the minimum three datapoints required for meaningful median analysis. While the broader AI & Software sector contains sufficient participants, filtering to narrow peer criteria eliminated sufficient comparability. Relying on an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable noise given Palantir's scale and market positioning relative to earlier-stage private competitors.

The $312.5B public valuation reflects market-determined pricing but lacks triangulation support from traditional comps methodologies. Key uncertainties center on the appropriate peer reference frame—whether Palantir should benchmark against the fragmented private AI firms (which operate at substantially earlier funding stages) or against other public software and data infrastructure companies outside the narrow AI sector definition. Valuation confidence remains limited without additional methodological leverage or a more densely-populated comparable set at similar scale and stage.
